body.statement: If \(d=\max_j|V(T_j)|\), all three problems in \(\text{def:k-fiber-problems}\) are solvable in \(d^K\operatorname{poly}(N,K)\) time by branching on the root signatures of a component with empty locus and deduplicating terminal root tuples.
body.justification: This proves a nontrivial FPT boundary and rules out hardness gadgets built only from bounded-size components.
body.gap: Generic minimum-label hardness allows unrestricted choice systems and does not respect the bounded root domain induced by a forest component.
body.consumer: Sparse applications with uniformly small chain components obtain exact root and ambiguity recovery even if the unrestricted \(K\)-frontier is hard.
